screens_reviewed: Single capture of the Audit step-1 (Context) screen in light theme: native stack header with place name + 'Context', a 'Step 1 of 9' pill, an 'Audit progress' card, the 9 step-jump pills, the 'Visit details' card (read-only auditor ID + audit date, first choice question), and the absolutely-positioned Back / Save & exit / Next footer.
verdict: A dense but coherent survey-wizard step that is on-brand (green-on-cream) and uses the shared design tokens consistently; the native header clears the Dynamic Island and the footer respects the home-indicator inset. The most visible problem is the three-up footer where 'Save & exit' is clipped to 'Save…' on iPhone width, and there is heavy redundancy of the 'Step N of 9' indicator (header + pill + progress card). Tap targets and contrast read fine.

critical_issues.location: FooterNav — three flex:1 buttons in one XStack
critical_issues.issue: The footer lays out Back, Save & exit, and Next as three equal flex={1} buttons in a single XStack with gap=$2.5 and only 15px horizontal screen padding. At iPhone width the 'Save & exit' label does not fit and is truncated to 'Save…' (visible in the screenshot), which is ambiguous (could read as a plain 'Save'). flexWrap='wrap' does not help because all three fit on one row width-wise; only the label text is clipped.
critical_issues.evidence: image (footer shows 'Save…'); audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1683 (XStack gap="$2.5" flexWrap="wrap") and :1701-1717 (Save & exit Button flex={1})
critical_issues.fix: On phone (layout.isTablet === false) stack the footer actions vertically, or drop one button to a second row: e.g. put Next full-width on top and Back + Save & exit on a second row, or shorten the label to 'Save' with the Save icon already present. Alternatively give Next more weight (flexBasis) and let Back/Save share a row so each label has room.

improvements.location: StepHeader — 'Step 1 of 9' pill + 'Audit progress / Step 1 of 9' card
improvements.suggestion: The same 'Step 1 of 9' fact is shown three times in the top third of the screen: the native header secondary line context, the rounded 'Step 1 of 9' pill (line ~606), and again as the body of the 'Audit progress' card (line ~651). Collapse to one: keep the 'Audit progress' card (which also carries the 'Setup and weighting' phase chip) and drop the standalone pill, recovering vertical space on a content-dense step.
improvements.evidence: image (Step 1 of 9 appears in pill and in Audit progress card); audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:606 and :651

improvements.suggestion: All nine step pills render with the same single brand tone (getStepTone returns one tone for every step) and the active one is only differentiated by a slightly stronger surface/border plus disabled state. In the screenshot the active 'Context' pill is barely distinguishable from inactive pills, so users get weak feedback on where they are in a 9-step flow. Add a clearer active treatment (filled primary, or a small check/index marker) to strengthen orientation.
improvements.evidence: image (Context pill nearly identical to others); audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1774-1782 (getStepTone is step-agnostic) and :685-689 (active only swaps surface/border)

improvements.suggestion: Most text in this screen sets fixed numeric fontSize (e.g. title fontSize={30} line 614, card title fontSize={22} line 1094, question fontSize={16} line 1169) and does not multiply by the stored fontScale preference the way YeeStackHeaderTitle does (it applies designSystem.fontScale). Users who raise the accessibility text size get a header that scales but body/question text that does not, producing inconsistent scaling. Consider routing these through ScaledText or applying fontScale.

The screen imports the static `designSystem` (light tokens) at line 23 rather than the live `useDesignSystem()` hook, so it always renders the light palette regardless of the auditor's theme preference. This light capture looks correct, but in dark mode the survey step would stay light while the rest of the app (and the native header via useYeeStackHeaderOptions) follows the resolved theme, causing a jarring light/dark seam. Switch to useDesignSystem() for theme-aware tokens.
improvements.evidence: audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:23 (import { designSystem }) vs lib/design-system.ts:501 useDesignSystem; useYeeStackHeaderOptions.ts:1995 uses live hook

tamagui_notes: design_system_components_used is (none): this screen hand-rolls every primitive (Card, QuestionCard, SelectionButton, Badge-like pills, progress bar) inline from raw YStack/XStack/Text rather than using shared components/ui/* such as Badge — confirmed by the pack header line 4 and the absence of ui imports in audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx.

SelectionButton is intentionally an XStack-pressable, not Tamagui Button, with a documented reason (Button pins a fixed size-token height that clipped multi-line labels) — audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1284-1287. Reasonable, but it means selection rows do not inherit the shared button radius/press tokens centrally.

Many style props are split between Tamagui shorthand and a raw `style={{}}` object (e.g. boxShadow, backgroundColor, borderColor) instead of theme tokens, e.g. Card line 1084-1088 — works, but bypasses Tamagui's token system the core defines.
platform_notes: Safe-area top: handled by the native stack header (useYeeStackHeaderOptions, headerShown:true) plus app/_layout.tsx Stack contentStyle paddingTop:20; the screenshot shows the place-name/Context header clearing the Dynamic Island. Not a bug.

Safe-area bottom: FooterNav is position:absolute with paddingBottom: insets.bottom + 12 (audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1680) and the scroll content reserves footerHeight + 48 (line 435), so the home indicator is respected and content is not hidden behind the footer.
Thumb reach: primary 'Next' CTA sits in the bottom-right of the fixed footer — good for right-handed thumb reach. The three-up footer is the only ergonomic concern (see footer-save-label-clipped).

Compact-fit: screen reads useResponsiveLayout() and getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (lines 85,434) and uses layout.screenPaddingHorizontal for the footer (line 483) rather than a hardcoded value — phone padding (15) comes from PHONE_LAYOUT_TOKENS, so it is responsive-aware.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios (mutedForeground #6B706F description text on cream surfaces looks near the AA threshold but cannot be measured precisely from the capture).
Behavior of the autosave/'Sync note' NoticeCard and the unanswered-question confirm Alert — runtime states not shown in this single capture.
How the footer reflows on iPad / wider widths and whether 'Save & exit' fits there (only the iPhone capture was provided).
score_rationale: Solid, on-brand, token-consistent step with correct safe-area handling and responsive padding, so it sits in the 7-8 band. It is held to 7 rather than 8 by one real visible defect (the clipped 'Save…' footer label on iPhone width) plus polish items (triple step-of-9 redundancy, weak active-step affordance, and the static light-only palette that would break in dark mode).
